walkthroughs.body_html:
HL Extension: Philosophy of Religion (Arguments for/against God, Religious Language, Religious Experience) — a core area of Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

HL Extension: Philosophy of Religion (Arguments for/against God, Religious Language, Religious Experience) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with HL Extension: Philosophy of Religion (Arguments for/against God, Religious Language, Religious Experience).

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Rudolf Otto
Friedrich Schleiermacher
Mircea Eliade

options: John of the Cross

Ignatius Loyola
Francisco Suarez

mcqs.q: Why do Jews not accept Jesus as the Messiah?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Because the Jewish Messiah is expected to bring peace, rebuild the Temple and restore Israel — events the Jewish tradition holds Jesus did not accomplish.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Because Jews believe Jesus never existed.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.

mcqs.q: What does Kant's categorical imperative require?
options: Because Jesus was crucified, and the Messiah cannot die.
Do whatever your conscience tells you to do.
Acting only on maxims you could will to be universal laws, and treating people as ends in themselves, never merely as means.
Treat others how you would like to be treated.
